data_classes.rule: Tenant and actor are taken only from the verified server session; clients receive hashes, not native actor identifiers.
A raw path exists only inside the process that selected or created the file and never crosses IPC, HTTP, UI, audit, or logging boundaries.

Bytes use bounded streaming into the API and bounded binary content channels only. The API may materialize only within a hard cap before fixed-origin multipart delivery. Bytes never enter JSON, renderer state, receipts, audit metadata, or logs.
Desktop session material stays in the owning main or broker process and Vault provider credentials stay server-side.
Object keys, buckets, storage URIs, unrestricted URLs, and long-lived signed URLs are never client-visible.
Subjects, bodies, recipients, mailbox addresses, provider item IDs, and draft IDs are absent from common receipts and logs; target identities are hashed.
Every successful export or attachment binds document_id, version_id, file_object_id, sha256, byte_size, and mime_type; latest substitution is forbidden.

allowed_inputs: selected path held in process memory
forbidden_outputs: raw path or bytes to logs
raw tenant or actor identity in a client receipt
authorization based only on AMIC OS role names

allowed_inputs: bounded bytes from authenticated local broker
publisher and process verified Named Pipe request
forbidden_outputs: raw path or bytes to logs
raw path over IPC or HTTP

crossings.payload: closed command and untrusted safe selectors
invariants: main returns an opaque handle only
raw path and bytes do not cross
no action occurs on item selection

crossings.payload: bounded authenticated binary body and operation ID
invariants: tenant and actor are server-derived
hash and byte size are verified
retry uses the same server nonce
API materialization never exceeds the configured hard cap

crossings.payload: mapped native identity, exact selectors, strict multipart metadata and bounded file bytes, correlation
invariants: Vault rechecks permission, Ethical Wall, Records, and DLP
Vault owns document, version, file object, bytes, hash, and audit
missing authority fails closed

crossings.payload: untrusted exact-version selector and hashed compose target
invariants: ItemChanged performs zero login, readiness, Vault network, or processing
server reauthorizes the exact version
cancel leaves the draft unchanged

crossings.payload: versioned local request, installation proof, nonce, hashed compose target
invariants: publisher, process, SID, nonce, expiry, and schema are verified
native receives no session token or private key
startup and item selection perform zero network work

crossings.payload: authenticated exact-version request and installation binding
invariants: interaction appears only for authoritative interaction-required
grant is one-time and short-lived
replay cannot redownload or reattach

crossings.payload: bounded byte stream plus exact hash and size
invariants: native verifies the stream before Attachments.Add
native creates and owns the protected temp path internally
the path never crosses IPC or enters a receipt

crossings.trigger: verified stream materialization for Outlook Attachments.Add
crossings.payload: exact bytes inside the native process boundary
invariants: current-user ACL is applied before content is written
path traversal and reparse points are rejected
success, cancel, crash, and reboot cleanup are additive audit stages

never_included: mail subject, body, recipient, mailbox, provider item ID, or draft ID
receipt.replay_rule: Same idempotency key hash and request fingerprint returns the existing receipt with should_execute false; any changed fingerprint is a conflict.
receipt.transition_rule: Stages are append-only and flow-ordered; an exact replay is not appended, save operations expose no exact version before promotion, exact version identity never changes, and cleanup is the only append after a terminal failure.

negative_matrix.attack: raw local or protected temp path in IPC, UI, HTTP, audit, or log payload
access, refresh, ID, session, provider, or grant token in a public payload
storage locator, unrestricted URL, or long-lived signed URL in a client payload
client-supplied tenant, actor, user, role, scope, capability, or permission decision
raw document bytes or a binary container in JSON, receipt, audit, or log payload
mail PII or provider compose identity in a common receipt
same idempotency scope reused with a changed request fingerprint
success receipt without exact document, version, file object, hash, size, and MIME identity
automatic latest substitution or exact-version identity change during one operation
stage skip, regression, post-cleanup mutation, or non-cleanup append after failure
